# A main module at go 1.28 or later is strict by default.
# "strict off" in go.mod turns it off; //go:nostrict exempts one file.
# Strictness crosses the packages of the module.

go list -m -f '{{.Strict}}'
stdout true

go build ./...
go vet ./...
go test ./...

# A nil misuse fails the build and vet.
cp bad.go.txt bad.go
! go build .
stderr 'strict: cannot use nil as \*lib.Node value'
stderr 'strict: f may be nil here; check f != nil first'
! go vet .
stderr 'strict: cannot use nil as \*lib.Node value'

# //go:nostrict exempts the file.
cp nostrict.go.txt bad.go
go build .
go vet .

# strict off turns the default off; the cached results must not be reused.
cp bad.go.txt bad.go
cp go.mod.off go.mod
go list -m -f '{{.Strict}}'
stdout false
go build .
go vet .
go mod tidy
go mod edit -fmt
grep '^strict off$' go.mod

# Back to strict: the build fails again.
cp go.mod.on go.mod
! go build .
stderr 'strict: cannot use nil as \*lib.Node value'

# A module before go 1.28 is not strict.
cp go.mod.old go.mod
go list -m -f '{{.Strict}}'
stdout false

-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.28
-- go.mod.on --
module example.com/m

go 1.28
-- go.mod.off --
module example.com/m

go 1.28

strict off
-- go.mod.old --
module example.com/m

go 1.27
-- lib/lib.go --
package lib

type Node struct{ N int }

func New(n int) *Node { return &Node{N: n} }

// Pick is a strict generic function: its result keeps its type argument.
func Pick[P any](a, b P) P { return a }
-- lib/lib_test.go --
package lib

import "testing"

func TestNew(t *testing.T) {
	if New(2).N != 2 {
		t.Fatal("bad")
	}
}
-- main.go --
package main

import "example.com/m/lib"

func use(n *lib.Node) int { return n.N }

func main() {
	n := lib.New(3)
	println(use(n), n.N, use(lib.Pick(n, n)))
}
-- bad.go.txt --
package main

import (
	"example.com/m/lib"
	"os"
)

func bad() {
	var p *lib.Node = nil
	_ = p
	f, _ := os.Open("x")
	f.Close()
}
-- nostrict.go.txt --
//go:nostrict

package main

import (
	"example.com/m/lib"
	"os"
)

func bad() {
	var p *lib.Node = nil
	_ = p
	f, _ := os.Open("x")
	f.Close()
}
